meta.description: Infers developmental trajectories, pseudotime, RNA velocity, and directed fate probabilities from single-cell data using PAGA, Slingshot, Monocle3, DPT, Palantir, scVelo, and CellRank 2. Use when ordering cells along a differentiation continuum, choosing a trajectory method by topology, rooting pseudotime, estimating RNA velocity direction, computing fate probabilities near a bifurcation, or judging whether an inferred trajectory is real.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 18 references (Wolf 2019 PAGA, Street 2018 Slingshot, Cao 2019 Monocle3, Setty 2019 Palantir, Saelens 2019 benchmark, Weiler 2024 CellRank2, Bergen 2020/2021, Weinreb 2018/2020, Gorin 2022, Zheng 2023, Soneson 2021, etc.) are real, correctly attributed papers; no fabricated statistics, DOIs, or trial results found across any of the 7 executed/evaluated outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Population-level computational biology methodology only; no individual diagnostic/prescriptive claims; out of clinical scope entirely, no disclaimer required.

methodological_ground.detail: Unusually rigorous methodological framing (pseudotime-is-not-time, root-sensitivity, probabilistic vs hard branch calls, Weinreb 2018 gauge-freedom non-identifiability) empirically validated by this audit: Palantir and CellRank both showed fate-probability entropy correctly falling from progenitor to committed cells on real data, and DPT/Slingshot pseudotime correctly increased from an orthogonally-anchored root.

code_usability.detail: Every one of the 6 code-based inputs was ultimately brought to a correct, real-data-validated result, so code is not wholesale unrunnable -- but 2 of scVelo's 3 documented velocity modes (the library default 'stochastic' and the Skill-recommended 'dynamical') crash with no call-site-level recovery against the declared-compatible scvelo 0.3.4 + a modern numpy/pandas stack (see Input 4 and P1 recommendations); CellRank's fate-probability block needed 3 undocumented fixes to complete on real branching data (Input 6).

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive real coverage of topology (PAGA), pseudotime (DPT), fate probabilities (Palantir, CellRank), R methods (Slingshot, Monocle3, tradeSeq) and RNA velocity (scVelo); method-selection guidance well matched to real topology types. Docked 1 pt: the RNA Velocity section's central code is correct in principle but 2 of its 3 documented modes are broken against the version it declares compatible.

reliability.note: The 'Version Compatibility' preamble (introspect installed API, adapt rather than retry) is a genuinely useful, uncommon recovery mechanism and worked for several drift issues hit during this audit. Docked for the scVelo dynamical/stochastic mode failures, which are not adaptable from the call site and leave the agent with no documented fallback beyond the least-recommended mode.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is ~207 lines for a 7-method Complex skill -- concise relative to its real scope; no padding found.

agent_usability.note: Governing Principle + Method Decision Table + Common Errors table (symptom/cause/fix format) are exemplary agent-usability design; Input 7 (adversarial) confirmed an agent grounded in this Skill correctly resists a velocity-confidence over-trust trap using exactly this content. Docked for the undocumented real-data failure modes hit in Inputs 3, 4, 5, 6.

human_usability.note: Clear structure, cross-linked Related Skills, real citations throughout.

security.note: No credentials, no unsafe eval/exec patterns, no destructive operations in any reviewed or executed code.

maintainability.note: Both shipped example files (monocle3_trajectory.R, scvelo_velocity.py) exist as documented (gate 8 pass). scvelo_velocity.py's core calls (scv.pp.filter_and_normalize with n_top_genes, scv.read for loom loading) are broken against the version scvelo 0.3+ the file itself declares -- has not been kept in sync with its target library.

agent_specific.note: Long, precise frontmatter description gives strong trigger precision; usage-guide.md separates prompts/tips from SKILL.md's technical depth well (good progressive disclosure); Related Skills give real composability. Docked slightly: frontmatter declares primary_tool: Monocle3, in tension with the body's explicit topology-first 'no single method wins' philosophy, and Monocle3 is also the single hardest of the 7 documented methods to install (GitHub-only, fails on Windows per this audit's own tooling log).

inputs.label: CellRank 2 GPCCA directed fate mapping on real branching data (Paul15)
inputs.note: SKILL.md's 'Directed Fate Mapping With CellRank 2' block needed 3 undocumented fixes to complete on real data with cellrank 2.3.3 (isolated venv, since cellrank would downgrade the shared venv's scipy per TOOLS.md): (1)(2) PseudotimeKernel.compute_transition_matrix() and compute_fate_probabilities() both spawn worker processes via multiprocessing.Manager(), which raises RuntimeError on Windows unless the calling script is guarded with if __name__=='__main__': (a general Windows/Python requirement, not cellrank-specific, but hit twice by this exact code); (3) predict_initial_states(n_states=1) as literally documented (no allow_overlap) raised ValueError: 30 cells overlapped between predicted initial and terminal states on this real branching data. key_strengths: Exceptionally rigorous, literature-grounded methodological framing (pseudotime-is-not-time, root sensitivity, probabilistic vs. hard branch calls, Weinreb 2018 gauge-freedom non-identifiability) that this audit empirically validated: Palantir and CellRank both showed fate-probability entropy correctly falling from progenitor to committed cells on real hematopoietic data.

The 'Version Compatibility' preamble (introspect the installed API, adapt rather than retry) is a rare, genuinely useful design feature that successfully guided recovery from several real API-drift issues encountered during this audit.

PAGA, DPT, and Palantir code blocks ran completely unmodified against real Paul et al. 2015 hematopoietic progenitor data and produced biologically correct, perfectly deterministic results (bit-for-bit reproducible across independent runs, no seed set anywhere in the documented code).

Method Decision Table (topology-first, grounded in Saelens 2019's 45-method benchmark) correctly steered this audit toward Slingshot and CellRank for real branching data, both of which correctly recovered multi-lineage structure (5 and 7 lineages respectively) once given proper inputs.

The Common Errors table is unusually well-designed defensive documentation -- the adversarial input (Input 7) confirmed an agent grounded in this Skill correctly resists a velocity-confidence over-trust trap using exactly this table's guidance.

recommendations.title: 2 of 3 documented scVelo velocity modes are broken against the Skill's own declared-compatible version
recommendations.problem: mode='dynamical' (SKILL.md line 157, the mode explicitly instructed instead of the default) and mode='stochastic' (scvelo's own default) both crash with real tracebacks against installed scvelo 0.3.4 -- the exact version range ('scVelo 0.3+') SKILL.md and examples/scvelo_velocity.py declare. recover_dynamics fails inside scvelo's own make_unique_list on a pandas-3.x incompatibility (confirmed unrecoverable via two call-site workarounds); velocity(mode='stochastic') fails inside leastsq_generalized on a numpy-2.x incompatibility. Only mode='deterministic', the least-recommended 'quick first pass' option, works.
recommendations.root_cause: scvelo 0.3.x's internal utilities were not updated for numpy>=2 / pandas>=3, and the Skill's compatibility note was never re-verified against a current numpy/pandas stack.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit fallback note to the RNA Velocity section and to examples/scvelo_velocity.py: if recover_dynamics or velocity(mode='stochastic') raise TypeError/ValueError referencing pandas 'unique' or numpy array assignment, fall back to mode='deterministic' and use scv.tl.velocity_pseudotime instead of scv.tl.latent_time (which requires recover_dynamics). Also fix the shipped scv.pp.filter_and_normalize(adata, min_shared_counts=20, n_top_genes=2000) call (SKILL.md line 154, examples/scvelo_velocity.py line 13) -- n_top_genes is not accepted by filter_and_normalize in current scvelo; do HVG selection via a separate sc.pp.highly_variable_genes call after log1p.

recommendations.title: CellRank's documented fate-mapping block needs 3 undocumented fixes to complete on real branching data
recommendations.problem: predict_initial_states(n_states=1) as literally written (SKILL.md line 111, no allow_overlap) raised ValueError on real data (30 cells overlapped between predicted initial and terminal macrostates). Separately, PseudotimeKernel.compute_transition_matrix() and compute_fate_probabilities() both spawn worker processes via multiprocessing.Manager(), which raises RuntimeError on Windows when the documented code is run as a plain .py script without an if __name__=='__main__': guard.
recommendations.root_cause: The documented code block was written/tested in a context (likely an interactive notebook, or non-Windows, or data where states happened not to overlap) that doesn't surface either failure mode; neither is mentioned in the text.
recommendations.fix: Add allow_overlap=True (or a one-line note on handling the ValueError) to the predict_initial_states example, and add a short Windows note near the CellRank and RNA Velocity code blocks: standalone .py scripts using cellrank/scvelo's parallel routines need if __name__=='__main__': guarding (or n_jobs=1) on Windows.

recommendations.title: PAGA's documented isolated-cluster heuristic does not distinguish real discrete cell types from a continuum
recommendations.problem: The Governing Principle's rule 2 and the Common Errors table both operationalize the continuum-vs-discrete decision as 'isolated clusters with no surviving connectivity edges are discrete cell types.' On real, genuinely discrete PBMC 1k data (T/B/NK/Mono/Platelet), 0 of 15 leiden clusters were isolated at the documented threshold=0.03, and even sweeping the threshold up to 0.5 isolated only 1/15 (median real connectivity value 0.29).
recommendations.root_cause: A single low, fixed threshold on PAGA connectivity is not, by itself, a reliable discrete-vs-continuum test on real data; the Method Decision Table already notes PAGA's 'threshold is manual; resolution-dependent' but the Governing Principle and Common Errors table present the isolated-cluster check as if it were sufficient on its own.
recommendations.fix: Add a caveat next to the PAGA continuum-test code: sweep the threshold and inspect the connectivity value distribution (not just cluster isolation at one fixed value), and treat PAGA connectivity as one input to a continuum judgment that should also draw on marker-based cell-type identity, not a standalone automatic test.

recommendations.title: tradeSeq's fitGAM silently requires raw counts, not the matrix already in hand from Slingshot/clustering
recommendations.problem: The text says 'downstream DE goes through tradeSeq (fitGAM then associationTest...)' immediately after the Slingshot code block, implying continuity, but fitGAM raised 'All values of the count matrix should be non-negative' when given the same scaled/log-transformed matrix used for clustering/UMAP.
recommendations.root_cause: The Slingshot and tradeSeq code blocks are presented back-to-back without stating that tradeSeq's counts argument must be the untouched raw count matrix, not the normalized/scaled matrix used upstream.
recommendations.fix: Add one line before or in the tradeSeq mention: 'fitGAM needs raw counts (assay(sce, "counts") or equivalent), not the scaled matrix used for clustering/UMAP.'

recommendations.title: Frontmatter primary_tool: Monocle3 is the hardest of the 7 documented methods to install and is in tension with the body's own topology-first philosophy
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md declares primary_tool: Monocle3, but Monocle3 (and its SeuratWrappers dependency) are GitHub-only R packages that fail to install on Windows (confirmed by this corpus's own tooling agent after a dedicated attempt logged in TOOLS.md). The body text itself argues against any single default method ('Methodology evolves... no single method wins across all topologies,' Saelens 2019).
recommendations.root_cause: The frontmatter metadata field appears to have been filled with a single representative tool name without reconciling it against the Skill's own topology-first, multi-method design.
recommendations.fix: Either drop primary_tool or change it to reflect the actual entry point (PAGA, since Governing Principle rule 2 calls it 'the mandatory first step' for every topology).
